neighbours.label: a list, not yet a pattern: the piece 'foot' completing 'Barefoot' / 'barefoot', and ' zone' / ' zones' right after 'dead'
fire: Farm runoff creates a huge dead zone off the coast every summer.
The children ran barefoot along the sandy path to the lake.
Scientists mapped several dead zones in the Baltic Sea last year.
He ordered a bottle of Barefoot wine for the picnic.
Our radio went silent as we drove into a dead zone between the hills.
She prefers to practice yoga barefoot on a wooden floor.
Fish cannot survive in the dead zones near the river mouth.
The band played a song called Barefoot Blues at the fair.
quiet: Farm runoff creates a huge algae bloom off the coast every summer.
The children ran in sandals along the sandy path to the lake.
Scientists mapped several climate zones in the Baltic region last year.
He ordered a bottle of sparkling wine for the picnic.
Our radio went silent because of a dead battery between the hills.
She prefers to practice yoga on one foot on a wooden floor.
Fish cannot survive among the dead leaves near the river mouth.
The band played a song called Bare Hands at the fair.

notes: Probes: 'dead zone' 0.78, 'barefoot' 0.52, 'Barefoot' 0.92, 'Hazelden' 0.85; 'time zone' 0.01; but 'Dead ends' 0.43 and 'dead spot' 0.18, so part of the 'dead' reading may come from 'dead' + noun rather than ' zone'. I could not find what Barefoot, dead zone and Hazelden share, so the label stays a list.
